cards.speaker: James
cards.text: I want a recipe at rank five. You have recipes at rank three or better, so the last two ranks are the only gap. Rank five is the best a piece can be made, and a firm that has one can fairly say it's passed the Guild's standard, not met it.

cards.speaker: James
cards.text: Master a recipe, take it to rank five. Two, if you can. You've already got work at rank three or above, so you know the cost of those last steps. A mastered recipe gives us pieces the Guild's own benches can't beat, and I'd like that on the record.

cards.speaker: James
cards.text: Bring one recipe to rank five this week. It's the top of the scale. Mastery is what lets us say we're better than the Guild and have a bench to prove it. You're close enough that it would be a waste to stop at three.

cards.speaker: James
cards.text: Take a recipe to rank five. We have work at rank three or better, so this is finishing, not starting. The Guild calls its masters a standard. I'd like us to be the standard, and one mastered recipe is the proof.
